_meta.note: Hand-authored Korean catalog: Seoul, Busan, Daegu, Incheon, Gwangju and Daejeon. Shaped like Qloo Insights entities plus a `_syn` block used for scoring and stripped before serving. Entity ids are fake. Not Qloo data.

properties.short_description: The Queen of Elegy: 'Camellia Lady' (동백아가씨, 1964), 'Island Village Teacher', the trot voice of a generation.
'Autumn Letter' (가을 편지), 'Farewell' (이별), 'Seoul Hymn': Korea's first singer at Carnegie Hall.
'Nim-gwa Hamkke' (님과 함께, 1972), 'A Farmer's Heart'; the Elvis of Korea.
'Muddy Stream of Tears' (1973), 'Hometown Station', 'Tess': the rival of Nam Jin and the emperor of trot.
'Come Back to Busan Port' (돌아와요 부산항에, 1976), 'Short Hair', 'The Woman Outside the Window': the King of Korean pop.
'Turn Around at Samgakji' (돌아가는 삼각지, 1967), 'Foggy Jangchungdan Park': the husky voice lost at 29.
'Be Strong, Geum-sun' (굳세어라 금순아, 1953), 'Shilla's Moonlit Night': the voice of the refugees in Busan.
'Tears of Mokpo' (목포의 눈물, 1935), the first great Korean pop record.
'Nim-eun Meon Gose' (님은 먼곳에, 1970), 'Coffee Once More': Shin Joong-hyun's soul singer.
'Beautiful Rivers and Mountains', 'Mi-in' (미인, 1974): the godfather of Korean rock and his guitar.
'Cup of Coffee' (커피 한잔, 1968), 'Nima': the sister duo in miniskirts, Shin Joong-hyun's first stars.
'Whale Hunting' (고래사냥, 1975), 'Why Did You Call Me' (왜 불러): the Twin Folio singer with the beard.
'Morning Dew' (아침 이슬, 1971), 'Evergreen Tree': the folk voice that became the song of the protests.
'Morning Dew', 'Friend': the student songwriter whose records were banned and sung anyway.
'That's You' (당신은 모르실거야, 1975), 'The Third Han River Bridge': the 1970s' sweet voice.
'Already Now' (아니 벌써, 1977), 'My Heart Is a Lake': the three Kim brothers and Korean psychedelic rock.
The child star of 1961 who became the trot queen of the 1970s: 'Dream in Mulbangagol', 'Daughter of the Sea'.
'Fog' (안개, 1967), 'Flower Path': the first Korean singer to win an international song festival.
'Wedding Dress' (우리 애인은 올드미스), 'A Pebble on the Road': the low baritone of the sixties.
'Red Sunset' (붉은 노을, 1988), 'Old Love': the ballad king of the late 1980s.
